verdict.line: You lose if Irelia lands E and chains into a marked Q before level 6; you win once W (Purge) and E (Disdain) are both online and she's forced to fight at point-blank range.

brief.thesis: Urgot vs Irelia sits at 50.8% over 859 games, but the shape is defensive — Irelia has both the lane and solo-kill edge because her Q (Bladesurge) and E (Flawless Duet) let her dictate when the fight happens, while Urgot's only pre-6 answer is a single rank of Q (Corrosive Charge) and a slow-building W. The matchup flips once Urgot's W cooldown drops low enough to punish her for staying in range and E (Disdain) is up to physically remove her from the fight.

theirWindow.when: she lands E (Flawless Duet) on you
theirWindow.what: Getting caught between the two converging blades stuns and Marks you, which refreshes her Q (Bladesurge) on the follow-up hit and snowballs her passive attack-speed stacks. Disengage immediately rather than trading through the stun.

yourWindow.when: her Q (Bladesurge) is down (used on a minion)
yourWindow.what: Bladesurge needs a target and is her only gap-close/escape; if she spends it clearing a wave or repositioning, step up and poke with Q or autos for the 10-6s it's on cooldown (lower at higher rank).

start.why: Measured at 51.7% over 900 games and 87.6% pick rate — the sustain and damage help you survive early all-in attempts without a strong poke tool of your own yet.

boots.why: 52.9% over 818 games and the standard pick — Irelia's passive stacks attack speed off every spell hit, and Steelcaps flattens the resulting auto-attack damage once she's on top of you.

core.why: First item in the highest-sample core path (58.2% over 91 games); the armor shred matters against an on-hit skirmisher who wants to keep landing autos through her passive.
Second item in the same path — the bonus health and damage reduction buy you the extra survivability to actually land W (Purge) channels instead of dying mid-cast.
Third item in the 58.2%-over-91-games path — stacking resistances cap out her snowballing passive damage over a long fight.

situational.when: she's fed and leaning on sustained autos/on-hit damage
you want more engage speed to close gaps and stick Disdain
you need an early defensive item to survive all-ins before Cleaver completes
you're ahead and want more sustain and damage on top of the core

runes.keystoneWhy: Rewards landing consecutive hits on the same target, which lines up with W (Purge) prioritizing the champion you've recently struck — the vulnerability amplifies the channel's damage once she's locked in range.

summoners.why: Flash+Ignite is run in 85.3% of games at 50.6% — Ignite punishes the heal she gets off a hit Bladesurge and gives you lane-kill pressure once E (Disdain) lands. Exhaust+Flash shows a notably higher 61.1% WR on a small sample if you want more direct control over her all-in windows instead.

playing.title: Poke with Q, respect her ranges
playing.detail: Hold Corrosive Charge (800 range) to chip her from outside her 600-range Q and don't walk into the zone where her 850-range E can converge on you.

playing.title: Never trade through an unmarked E
playing.detail: If you get caught between the two blades of Flawless Duet you're stunned and Marked, which refreshes her Q on the follow-up hit. Back off the instant she throws it rather than fighting through the stun.

playing.title: Save E to physically remove her
playing.detail: Disdain (16/15.5/15/14.5/14s cooldown) stops on the first enemy champion it hits and hurls them away — use it to reset neutral spacing the moment she commits Q or W.

playing.title: Channel W once she's already stuck on you
playing.detail: Purge's self-slow barely matters when she's already at melee range post-dash; it prioritizes her as a recently-struck target and triggers Echoing Flames for extra damage.

playing.title: Punish Q spent on minions
playing.detail: Bladesurge requires a target; if she dashes a minion instead of you, her only gap-close is down for 10-6s depending on rank — step up and poke while she has no dash.

playing.title: Bank R for the execute, not the engage
playing.detail: Fear Beyond Death threatens from 2500 range once she's low, but its 100/85/70s cooldown means whiffing it or burning it defensively costs you tempo for the rest of the fight.

playing.title: Check her passive stacks before extending
playing.detail: Ionian Fervor stacks attack speed per spell hit and adds bonus on-hit damage at max stacks — if she's near cap mid-trade, disengage instead of continuing to exchange autos.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, rune, summoner, and win-rate numbers are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch (16.19.1); the ability mechanics, timing windows, and tactical reading are my own analysis built on top of that data.

stats.opponentTip: Keep an eye out for Irelia’s (P) and Conqueror stacks before fighting her. Focus on avoiding her (E) when contesting lane.
